Megan —

Thanks for sending the redline and the note. Quick read-through and our commercial asks:
- Governing law: Redwood prefers a single-state law to avoid multi-jurisdictional risk. We propose Washington (State of Washington) as a neutral operational seat given our regional infra.
- Venue/seat for injunctive relief: Redwood can accept a carve that permits either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in state/federal courts in King County, Washington, without waiving the requirement to arbitrate other disputes.
- Arbitration: Redwood prefers JAMS/AAA arbitration (commercial rules) with an agreed seat of Seattle, WA and expedited discovery protocols for high-severity claims.
- Equitable relief language: Redwood will accept a narrow carve for emergency relief (preservation and preliminary injunction) but needs an explicit no-waiver clause and a 7-day notice period for Redwood to attempt an alternative remedy (where practically possible).

I attached a tidy one-page proposal (RW_Proposed_Seat_Injunction_Carve.docx) with suggested contract text for Sections 16–18. If that aligns, we can turn this into tracked changes and loop in commercial for final signoff.

Markus / Kim —

A couple of drafting notes I recommend we include before sending a tracked copy back:
1) Narrow the injunctive carve: limit to relief necessary to prevent irreparable harm (IP/data preservation/compelled shutdown). Avoid a general "injunction" carve that invites forum shopping.
2) Service/notice: require Acme to give Redwood immediate notice and a 48-hour window to consent or propose alternative interim measures where facilities are implicated.
3) Forum selection fallback: where emergency relief is sought outside King County (for reasons of urgency), include a provision that disputes on jurisdiction for the balance of the claim will be stayed pending arbitration (so we don't get two-for-one litigation).
4) Confidentiality of proceedings: include an obligation that any public filings related to injunctive relief keep technical details and customer data redacted.

If we keep the seat in WA, we should be prepared to brief commercial on any cost impacts (legal + potential travel).

-Laura

Megan / Daniel —

Per attached proposal, Redwood will accept the following compromise for Sections 16–18:
- Governing law: State of Washington.
- Arbitration: Mandatory final resolution by arbitration administered by JAMS in Seattle, WA (commercial rules), except as to emergency equitable relief.
- Injunctive carve: Either party may seek provisional injunctive or preservation relief in the state or federal courts located in King County, WA, provided: (i) the seeking party gives prompt written notice to the other party (aiming for 48 hours where practicable); (ii) the seeking party files a short affidavit explaining urgency and scope; and (iii) the filing is limited to relief necessary to prevent irreparable harm to intellectual property, data integrity, or to avoid operational shutdowns.
- No-waiver clause: filing for emergency relief does not waive the obligation to arbitrate remaining claims; the court action will be limited to the emergency relief sought.

We can circulate tracked changes with the exact clause wording if Acme can confirm that King County/Seattle is acceptable as the local court seat for emergency relief. If Acme insists on New York as governing law, we need a brief internal risk memo on asset-side enforcement and forum costs before escalation.

Attached: RW_Proposed_Seat_Injunction_Carve.docx
